title: Brazil's Lula wins electoral court challenge against Meta for alleged pro-Bolsonaro algorithm bias
source_used: AP text via WTOP and Eagle-Tribune
key_facts: A judge of Brazil's top electoral court, Justice Marco Aurélio Bellizze, ruled on Thursday 15 Oct 2026 that Meta must immediately secure equal treatment of the two presidential candidates before the 25 Oct runoff.
The ruling follows a complaint by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's campaign accusing Meta (Instagram, Facebook, WhatsApp) of biased algorithms and AI restrictions favouring Flávio Bolsonaro.
Meta may not reduce the distribution of political content, restrict searches or remove posts in a way that creates an imbalance, and must make its AI tool apply identical criteria to both candidates.
Fine for non-compliance: 500,000 reais (about $98,000) per day.
Lula's campaign alleges unjustified reductions in reach and that WhatsApp's Meta AI would not generate campaign images of the 80-year-old president but would for Bolsonaro supporters.
On 11 Oct Meta told the court it rejects the accusations, admitted technical glitches affecting accounts beyond Brazil and said it complies with electoral rules.
Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, got 47% to Lula's 45% in the 4 Oct first round.
quote_evidence: A judge of Brazil's top electoral court ruled on Thursday that Meta must adopt measures to immediately secure equal treatment of the two presidential candidates ahead of an Oct. 25 runoff.
Bellizze said in his ruling that Meta must pay a fine of 500,000 reais ($98,000) per day if it fails to comply.
why_it_matters_hint: A court is directing how a major platform's feed and AI assistant treat candidates in a tight election.
notes: AP original blocked (403); same AP text read on WTOP and Eagle-Tribune. Ruling is an interim order on the campaign's allegations; Meta denies bias.
